segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of two highways which join one another'); the intersection i is the target region of the declared intention and the region whose entry ends the approach: the subject enters i at the observation e at which its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') having not overlapped it at the observation before. Its approach is 'a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection' (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), the carriers being lanes (st.lane) or the kinds refining them. st.intersection is 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line': no halt place is read. st.lane_enters is 'not a stand-in for ... the subject's presence in the intersection', which rel.occupies reads.

st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}'; the right turn lane of the approach is the turn lane t of side right that enters i (st.lane_enters) and that s6 selects. 'the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane': the approach ends and the turn begins at the subject's entry into i, and at the observation before that entry the subject's footprint overlaps t (rel.occupies). st.turn_lane refines st.lane, whose exclusion 'a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane' does not apply: lane membership is read by occupancy. The approach is read at its end and the turn at its start (narrowing disclosed): a lane change into t earlier on the approach is not a breach.

The words borrow subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223, which quotes: 'If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning'. The highway the subject approaches on has such a lane where exactly one st.turn_lane ('a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}') of side right enters i (st.lane_enters) and its designated direction (st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') is aligned with that of a lane the subject occupies entering i, the cosine of the angle between the two directions at or above p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos; turn lanes of other approaches to i point along other legs and are not the subject's highway's. 'single' is kept: a second such lane makes the condition false. 'used only for turning' is the turn lane's own kind. st.lane_direction is read normalised, as its contract says.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the right at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included
the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the right at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: 'as set forth in subsection 4' borrows only that subsection's description of the lane: a single right lane, provided by the highway's design, used only for turning (kept in s6 as exactly one right turn lane of the approach). Whether a right turn lane exists is a fact of the road, not a verdict: the lane is the right turn lane whether or not any vehicle in it complies with the subsection's duty to be driven there only to turn right, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with here.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: 'as set forth in subsection 4' borrows only that subsection's description of the lane: a single right lane, provided by the highway's design, used only for turning (kept in s6 as exactly one right turn lane of the approach). Whether a right turn lane exists is a fact of the road, not a verdict: the lane is the right turn lane whether or not any vehicle in it complies with the subsection's duty not to travel through an intersection, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with here.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation e is one at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies) and did not at the observation before (its entry). int.right_turn(subject, i) is declared true at the observation before e (the intention to turn, and the turn being a right turn, s2 and s4). At the observation before e the subject occupies a lane c that enters i (st.lane_enters c i), and there is exactly one st.turn_lane t of side right that enters i whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) makes with c's a cosine at or above p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos (the highway has a right turn lane, s6 with s7). Whether the event occurred is unknown where the observation before e does not show the subject's place (the subject's first observation, or no mapped carrier); a missing direction, kind or entrance makes the applicability unknown only where the verdict turns on it.
obligation: At the observation before e, the subject's footprint overlaps the right turn lane t (rel.occupies): the approach ends and the right turn is begun from t. Where the subject at the observation before e occupies t, the duty is met whatever else is unobserved; where it occupies no lane entering i that could be t, it is violated; where t's identity turns on an unobserved direction, it is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'the approach for the right turn and the right turn' are read at the observation before the entry into the intersection, where the approach ends and the turn begins: the subject must then be in the right turn lane. A lane change into it earlier on the approach is not a breach, and the turn is identified by the declared intention and the entry, not by a recognized heading change.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A single right st.turn_lane enters the intersection on the subject's approach; the subject, with int.right_turn declared at the intersection, occupies the adjacent through lane (same direction) at the observation before it enters the intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same layout; the subject occupies the right turn lane at the observation before it enters the intersection, with int.right_turn declared.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters the intersection with int.right_turn declared, but no right turn lane enters the intersection from its approach (only through lanes).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the source declares st.lane_direction absent, so whether the right turn lane belongs to the subject's approach is unknown and the subject is not in it.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A right turn lane enters the intersection on the subject's approach; the subject enters from the through lane with int.left_turn declared and no int.right_turn: the duty does not arise.

param_proposals.name: p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) between the designated directions of two mapped lanes entering one intersection at which they count as lanes of the same approach carrying traffic the same way: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way, far below the angle between the legs of a junction
param_proposals.source: map lane-direction noise; mirrors p.lane_opposed_direction_cos proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_307_8a_o2
